sources.what: 'ON FEBRUARY 27 1921'; 'At the time of the accident it was dark and the weather was clear'; No. 20 passed the home signal at stop and ran through the open derail, 'The train continued on the ties'; the coach struck 'was of wooden construction with steel center sills'; No. 151 about 50 mph; 35 passengers and 2 employees killed; direct cause 'failure of Engineman Long to observe and obey the signal indication of the home signal'; Long thought he saw a green light above a red one, then lost sight of it in smoke and steam; the derail, 311 feet from the crossing, did not give the protection intended
sources.who: Interstate Commerce Commission, Bureau of Safety, accident report (March 14, 1921)

sources.what: 'On Sunday evening, February 27'; westbound New York Central No. 151 (Interstate Express) and eastbound Michigan Central No. 20 (Canadian), both passenger trains; 'Thirty-seven persons were killed'; No. 20 ran past the home signal and through the derail, a day coach stood on the New York Central track; two-storey tower, the route was lined for the New York Central train
sources.who: Railway Age, March 4, 1921 (reprinted by michiganrailroads.com, with the ICC summary)

sources.what: the coroner's count: 'thirty-five (35) passengers and two (2) employees killed'; the ICC's cause; the route set for the New York Central train
sources.who: The Dash (Porter County history), 'Tragic Railroad Accidents in Porter County' (2024), quoting the coroner's report

sources.what: 'the railroad wreck at Porter which caused the death of thirty-seven persons' (Valparaiso newspapers, March 1921)
sources.who: Porter County Museum, Looking Back: March 1921

beats.text: 37 people died at one railroad crossing. In Porter, Indiana.
beats.label: PORTER, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: ICC accident report, 1921; Railway Age, 1921

beats.text: It was Sunday evening, February 27, 1921. Dark, and clear. Two passenger trains were headed for the same crossing.
beats.label: FEBRUARY 27, 1921

beats.text: The tower set the signals for the New York Central express. The Michigan Central train was told to stop.
beats.label: THE SIGNAL TOWER

beats.text: It didn't. It ran through a safety derail, onto the ties, and a wooden coach was on the crossing when the express arrived.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CENTRAL No. 20

beats.text: The express hit it at about 50 miles an hour.
beats.label: NEW YORK CENTRAL No. 151

beats.text: Federal investigators said the engineer missed a stop signal. He said he thought he saw green, then lost it in smoke and steam.
beats.label: WHAT INVESTIGATORS SAID

beats.text: They also said the derail, 311 feet from the crossing, did not give the protection it was meant to.
beats.label: THE DERAIL
